maya: heads up — customer on private VPC reported OOM+kernel oops after we pushed the 535->550 kernel module on their onprem hosts. they see CUDA init failures and `nvidia` kmod mismatch in dmesg. anyone seen this pattern recently?
kevin: ugh. likely driver vs kernel module ABI mismatch. did they use a distro kernel patch (backported symbols)?
sara: they mentioned they patched kernel for live-patching, and the customer's infra team recompiled a custom kernel. that often breaks nvidia kmod ABI.
raj: can we get the exact errors? ask for `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` and `modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic` and `nvidia-smi -q | grep \"Driver Version\"` — vendor kernel module vermagic mismatch is the tell.
maya: sent request. they returned: `nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout` and `failed to init NVML: Unknown Error (999)` plus `kernel: NVRM: API mismatch`.
kevin: yup API mismatch. typical cause: driver package expects different kernel headers. For private customers we need to document supported kernel ABI ranges and require kmod build logs.
sara: agree. also NCCL can silently degrade if partial driver load happens — performance regressions that look like network flakiness. we should warn support to check `nv_peer_mem` and `nvidia_uvm` statuses.
raj: immediate mitigations: 1) pin to older driver variant we know is binary-compatible, 2) suggest customer install distributed vendor driver instead of custom kmod, or 3) provide a signed kmod built against their kernel (if contract allows).
maya: customer asked about matrix — they want a definitive list of supported kernel versions per driver per distro. we don't have a single canonical matrix for onprem because customers compile kernels.
kevin: proposal: add a lightweight diagnostic script to our private onboarding that collects `uname -r`, `cat /proc/version`, `modinfo nvidia`, `lsmod | grep nvidia`, `dmesg | tail -n50` and flags common mismatch signatures. ship as `redwood-driver-check.sh`.
sara: +1. also we should update runbook: when API mismatch seen, escalate to eng-infra with the kmod build log, output of `modinfo`, and the kernel config (`/proc/config.gz` if available).
raj: I'll draft the runbook snippet and a minimal diagnostic script. can someone from support confirm contract constraints for building a kmod for a customer?
maya: pinging @engops-bot to open a support ticket and tag sales for contract check.
engops-bot: created ticket INF-9721 for customer acme-private-01, assigned to support-oncall. link: https://redwood.support/t/INF-9721
sara: also note capacity implication — if we fallback them to hosted variant temporarily, we may need burst dedicated capacity in the region to accept their traffic. ops, can we estimate cost for 2w of burst?
kevin: rough calc: 4x A100-equivalent for 2w ~ estimate $18k on reserved/dedicated costs. add that to ticket as escalation option.
maya: thanks. raj + kevin please pair on runbook + diag script, sara will update support checklist, i'll coordinate with sales. closing loop once INF-9721 updates. :thumbsup:
